title: POC Hosting Rubric — KiteBridge Consult
next_steps: Redwood to share hosted vs dedicated cost model sheet
Customer to provide 1-week sample query trace and histogram of sequence lengths
action_items: Priya: export and share 7-day request log (anonymized) by 2027-06-29
Daniel (Redwood SE): prepare initial throughput/latency benchmark plan by 2027-06-30
Maya: send compliance pack (SOC2 summary, data-retention options) by 2027-06-27
meeting_header: Date: 2027-06-25 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (CTO, KiteBridge), Priya Narang (Lead ML Eng), Marco Ruiz (Infra), Sara Lim (PM)
summary: Initial POC scoping to decide hosting mode (hosted, dedicated, private) for KiteBridge's document-questioning assistant. Discussed success criteria (latency, accuracy, cost), workload sizing (qps, concurrency, token distribution), benchmark plan and timelines. Security and data residency constraints noted — strong preference for VPC/private for regulated clients but want to evaluate cost/latency tradeoffs first. Agreed next steps: share logs, schedule benchmark kick-off, Redwood to deliver cost model and compliance docs.
topics: Success criteria (p50/p95 latency, throughput, quality gates)
Workload sizing (qps, avg tokens, peak concurrency)
Benchmark plan (dataset, metrics, envs to test: hosted/dedicated/private)
transcript: [00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for taking the time. quick roll call?
[00:05] Liam: hi Liam here, CTO at KiteBridge
[00:07] Priya: Priya, lead ML
[00:09] Marco: Marco, infra
[00:11] Sara: Sara, product
[00:13] Daniel: Daniel from Redwood, SE, excited to dig in

[00:18] Maya: objective for today: agree on success criteria for the POC, get you the benchmark plan and define a timeline and what artifacts we need from you. also discuss hosting modes: hosted, dedicated, private — and decision criteria. sound right?

[00:29] Liam: yep that's perfect. we're trying to decide if we can start on your hosted offering or if we need dedicated or private from day one because of regulated clients. cost is a big factor too.

[00:41] Priya: to add — we have two workloads: short-chat style Q&A (avg 60 tokens request, 120 tokens response) and long-document retrieval assistant (avg 800 tokens output). Peak concurrency can be spiky during business hours. we expect 15 qps on average, spiking to maybe 80 qps for short bursts. these are rough numbers, we'll share real traces.
[01:05] Daniel: ok that's helpful. When you say 80 qps spikes, is that sustained for minutes or seconds? that affects autoscaling and batch sizing recommendations.

[01:15] Priya: usually seconds, sometimes minutes — like a few minutes when a campaign rolls out. latency targets: p50 under 200ms for short chat, p95 under 800ms. For long-doc we can accept p95 under 2s. Are those achievable on hosted?

[01:33] Maya: short answer: yes for many setups but depends on model size, quantization, batching, and whether KV/prefix caching helps. hosted has fastest time to test. Dedicated gives more predictable p95 under load. Private (VPC/on-prem) adds network overhead but gives you control for compliance. we'll propose a small benchmark matrix to validate your p50/p95 across modes.

[01:52] Marco: compliance note — two of our largest customers require data to live in their tenancy and use customer-managed KMS. also audit logs for every request. that pushes us toward private or a dedicated VPC with KMS integration.

[02:04] Maya: got it. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and on-prem options, and our Dedicated product can be set up in a VPC with KMS integration. we should capture which customers have that requirement; that becomes a gating criteria.
[02:18] Sara: what's the delta in cost for dedicated vs hosted usually? we don't need precise right now but rough order of magnitude would help for decisions.

[02:27] Daniel: ballpark — hosted charges per-token and scales; dedicated is reserved capacity so you commit monthly and get lower per-token cost for bursty steady traffic. private on-prem includes licensing + support. we'll send a cost model spreadsheet keyed to your qps and token distribution. note that quantization and batching changes effective cost by 20-60% depending on model.
[02:50] Priya: Benchmarking: we'd want to validate model accuracy/regression too. our concern is that quantized/dedicated variants don't regress on quality. how do you propose we measure that?

[03:02] Daniel: we usually have a test set of ~500 labeled prompts covering edge cases and golden outputs. we do an automated pass and compute exact-match, BLEU-ish heuristics, and human spot checks. we also track hallucination rates on a curated prompt set. for POC you can supply a prioritized prompt list.
[03:18] Liam: timeline — we need a recommendation within 3 weeks to present to execs. can Redwood deliver a bench report + decision rubric in that window?

[03:27] Maya: yes — proposed timeline: you share logs and prompt set by Mon (2027-06-29), Redwood runs bench and returns preliminary results by 2027-07-05, then an engineering benchmark session on 2027-07-07. decision playbook ready by 2027-07-12. does that fit?
[03:45] Marco: that's tight but doable. we'll need the infra checklist for dedicated/private so we can provision IPs and firewall rules before the 7th.

[03:55] Daniel: we'll attach the infra checklist with the kickoff calendar invite. for benchmarks we recommend testing three environments: Redwood Hosted (our public), Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool in region), and Private VPC (same cluster image but customer VPC). keep in mind the private path may need a couple extra days for networking and KMS set up.
[04:18] Priya: on workload sizing — we'll share histograms. quick Q: how do you handle prefix/KV cache — is that available on hosted?

[04:26] Daniel: yes hosted supports KV/prefix caching; we expose TTL and hit-rate stats. caching is particularly effective for your short-chat workload if many similar queries occur. that will help p50 a lot and reduce cost. caching in private behaves the same, but cache can be customer-managed if required.
[04:42] Sara: are there fallbacks if a model hits capacity? we don't want 5xxs for clients.

[04:47] Maya: Redwood has smart routing and fallback policies — you can route to a smaller/cheaper variant or queue with graceful degradation. we'll show a failure-mode playbook in the benchmark deliverable.
[04:58] Liam: security specifics — SOC2 is ok, but we also need SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs retained 13 months. can you confirm those?

[05:07] Daniel: yes we support SAML, granular RBAC, and configurable audit-log retention. some of the retention and export flows differ between hosted and private. I'll mark that as a gating question and include it in the compliance pack.

[05:20] Priya: I want to nail down the success criteria matrix now: performance, cost per 1M tokens, quality delta vs baseline model, security gating (KMS/audit). proposal: if hosted meets p95 targets and cost per token is <X, we go hosted; if hosted meets p95 but cost is >X and we need KMS, we go dedicated; if KMS+data residency mandatory, private. Is that the right high-level rubric?

[05:45] Maya: broadly yes. we'll help you set the exact numbers. sometimes it's also about risk tolerance — some enterprises prefer dedicated even if hosted meets numbers because of control. we'll include a decision tree for execs.
[05:58] Marco: on the data flow for private — do we need a VPN or can we do VPC peering?
[06:04] Daniel: both supported. VPC peering and private link endpoints available. for on-prem there's a different installer. we'll include the options in the infra checklist.
[06:15] Sara: what about observability — token-level cost breakdown per route, latency heatmaps?

[06:20] Daniel: Redwood Console provides token-level cost, per-route latency, model KV hit-rate, and tracing hooks. retention windows differ by plan but can be extended as an add-on. we'll show a demo later if helpful.
[06:33] Priya: can we run an initial micro-benchmark on hosted quickly just to get a sanity check? like 10k requests to measure p50/p95?
[06:39] Maya: absolutely. once you send the anonymized traces and sample prompts, we can run a smoke bench on hosted within 48 hours.
[06:48] Liam: any gotchas we should be aware of — like cold-starts, KV cache warmup?

[06:53] Daniel: yes cold-starts for very large models can add latency on first few requests depending on infra. for most workloads continuous warm traffic keeps instances hot; we also have warm-pools for dedicated. KV cache warming is important — we'll include a warmup script in the benchmark pack.
[07:08] Priya: quality regression risk — you mentioned quantization. are there standard quantization profiles you recommend?

[07:14] Daniel: we provide quantization profiles tested across families; for QA we usually run 8-bit quantize and a float fallback if we detect regressions above threshold. the Optimize tool recommends profiles per workload.
[07:27] Sara: will Redwood run the benchmarks or do we run them in our infra?

[07:31] Maya: both. Redwood will run hosted and dedicated tests; for private we'll provide scripts and can run jointly with your infra team. decision depends on what you prefer for trust and reproducibility.
[07:42] Liam: cost question again — is there a minimum commitment for dedicated?
[07:46] Daniel: yes typically a monthly reserved capacity commit—we'll outline tiers. smallest starting tier is often enough for an initial pilot but economics get better at higher commits.

[07:55] Priya: for the benchmark suite, here's what we want to measure: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, tail latency, model output similarity vs baseline, cost per 1k tokens, and KV cache hit-rate. please include warmup behavior in the report.

[08:12] Daniel: noted — we'll instrument those metrics and produce a single bench report comparing the three modes. we'll include charts: latency CDFs, cost per token, throughput curves by concurrency, and quality delta table.

[08:26] Maya: good — think about decision criteria: if hosted meets all performance and security constraints and cost is within 20% of dedicated, recommend starting hosted for faster time-to-value. if cost delta >20% and consistent high qps — recommend dedicated. if hard compliance gates (KMS/tenant isolation/data residency) then private. we'll codify this in the deliverable.
[08:47] Marco: curious — do you support model pinning and gradual rollouts? if we have a regression we need to roll back quickly.
[08:53] Daniel: yes rollout features, canary, automatic fallback. and we keep model version history so rollbacks are straightforward.
[08:59] Priya: any latency/network implications for region choices? we operate in EU and NA largely — need region-aware routing.
[09:05] Maya: Redwood routes by region and can pin requests to regions. we'll show sample routing configs in the playbook.
[09:13] Sara: ok timeline recap — you said we'll share logs by 6/29, Redwood bench by 7/5, engineering benchmark 7/7, decision 7/12. I'll put those in calendar and send invites.
[09:24] Liam: final question — if we choose hosted initially and later move to dedicated/private, is migration straightforward?
[09:30] Daniel: yes migration paths are built-in — same API surface, model pinning and rollout policies make migration smoother. we'll include a migration checklist.
[09:40] Maya: perfect. any final risks to call out?
[09:44] Priya: main risk: hidden cost from long-document outputs and retrieval overhead. we'll need to measure tokens per session carefully.
[09:52] Marco: networking delays for private could surprise latency numbers — important to test with real infra.
[09:58] Daniel: agreed. we'll shape the benchmark to mirror your real infra network path as much as possible.
[10:05] Maya: ok I'll summarize and send action items — thanks all. we'll follow up with the cost sheet and compliance pack.
[10:12] Liam: thanks everyone, bye
[10:14] Sara: thanks
[10:15] Priya: bye
